    42→    def __init__(self, id="-", name=None):
    43→        """A wrapper around the various forms of an Apple signing identity."""
    44→        self.id = id
    45→        if self.id == "-":
    46→            self.team_id = None
    47→            self.name = ADHOC_IDENTITY_NAME
    48→            self.profile = None

    54→    @classmethod

    56→        try:
    57→            return re.match(r".*\(([\dA-Z]*)\)", name)[1]

    59→            raise BriefcaseCommandError(
    60→                f"Couldn't extract Team ID from signing identity {name!r}"
    61→            )

    89→    def _install_app_requirements(
    90→        self,
    91→        app: AppConfig,
    92→        requires: list[str],
    93→        app_packages_path: Path,
    94→    ):
    95→        # Determine the min macOS version from the VERSIONS file in the support package.
    96→        versions = dict(
    97→            [part.strip() for part in line.split(": ", 1)]
    98→            for line in (
    99→                (self.support_path(app) / "VERSIONS")
   100→                .read_text(encoding="UTF-8")
   101→                .split("\n")
   102→            )
   103→            if ": " in line
   104→        )
   105→        support_min_version = Version(versions.get("Min macOS version", "11.0"))
   106→
   107→        # Check that the app's definition is compatible with the support package
   108→        macOS_min_version = Version(getattr(app, "min_os_version", "11.0"))
   109→        if macOS_min_version < support_min_version:
   110→            raise BriefcaseCommandError(
   111→                f"Your macOS app specifies a minimum macOS version of {macOS_min_version}, "
   112→                f"but the support package only supports {support_min_version}"
   113→            )
   114→
   115→        macOS_min_tag = str(macOS_min_version).replace(".", "_")
   116→
   117→        if getattr(app, "universal_build", True):
   118→            # Perform the initial install targeting the current platform
   119→            host_app_packages_path = (
   120→                self.bundle_path(app) / f"app_packages.{self.tools.host_arch}"
   121→            )
   122→            # A standard install, except we explicitly reject installs from source
   123→            # tarballs with `--only-binary :all:`. This is for two reasons:
   124→            #
   125→            # 1. Consistency. We need to use `--only-binary :all:` when we do the second
   126→            #    "other arch" wheel install because of use of the `--platform` argument;
   127→            #    if we only reject source tarballs from one of the installs, then a
   128→            #    package that only provides binary wheels for one architecture would
   129→            #    cause inconsistent results depending on which platform was the host;
   130→            #    and
   131→            #
   132→            # 2. Security. Installs from source tarball involve executing arbitrary code
   133→            #    at time of installation; and it makes the entire development
   134→            #    environment building the app a vector for introducing vulnerabilities
   135→            #    into an app. Forcing the use of binary wheels ensures that we can know
   136→            #    with certainty the provenance of any binary content in the app.
   137→            #
   138→            # Since Briefcase is a tool designed to produce redistributable binaries,
   139→            # we've made the judgement call that the (minor, with known workarounds)
   140→            # inconvenience of not being able to use source tarballs is outweighed by
   141→            # the need to produce reliable, repeatable binary artefacts.
   142→            super()._install_app_requirements(
   143→                app,
   144→                requires=requires,
   145→                app_packages_path=host_app_packages_path,
   146→                pip_args=[
   147→                    "--only-binary",
   148→                    ":all:",
   149→                    "--platform",
   150→                    f"macosx_{macOS_min_tag}_{self.tools.host_arch}",
   151→                ],
   152→            )
   153→
   154→            # Find all the packages with binary components.
   155→            # We can ignore any -universal2 packages; they're already fat.
   156→            binary_packages = self.find_binary_packages(
   157→                host_app_packages_path,
   158→                universal_suffix="_universal2",
   159→            )
   160→
   161→            # Now install dependencies for the architecture that isn't the host architecture.
   162→            other_arch = {
   163→                "arm64": "x86_64",
   164→                "x86_64": "arm64",
   165→            }[self.tools.host_arch]
   166→
   167→            # Create a temporary folder targeting the other platform
   168→            other_app_packages_path = (
   169→                self.bundle_path(app) / f"app_packages.{other_arch}"
   170→            )
   171→            if other_app_packages_path.is_dir():
   172→                self.tools.shutil.rmtree(other_app_packages_path)
   173→            self.tools.os.mkdir(other_app_packages_path)
   174→
   175→            if binary_packages:
   176→                with self.console.wait_bar(
   177→                    f"Installing binary app requirements for {other_arch}..."
   178→                ):
   179→                    self._pip_install(
   180→                        app,
   181→                        app_packages_path=other_app_packages_path,
   182→                        pip_args=[
   183→                            "--no-deps",
   184→                            "--platform",
   185→                            f"macosx_{macOS_min_tag}_{other_arch}",
   186→                            "--only-binary",
   187→                            ":all:",
   188→                        ]
   189→                        + [
   190→                            f"{package}=={version}"
   191→                            for package, version in binary_packages
   192→                        ],
   193→                        install_hint=f"""
   194→
   195→If an {other_arch} wheel has not been published for one or more of your requirements,
   196→you must compile those wheels yourself, or build a non-universal app by setting:
   197→
   198→    universal_build = False
   199→
   200→in the macOS configuration section of your pyproject.toml.
   201→""",
   202→                    )
   203→            else:
   204→                self.console.info("All packages are pure Python, or universal.")
   205→
   206→            # If given the option of a single architecture binary or a universal2 binary,
   207→            # pip will install the single platform binary. However, a common situation on
   208→            # macOS is for there to be an x86_64 binary and a universal2 binary. This means
   209→            # you only get a universal2 binary in the "other" install pass. This then causes
   210→            # problems with merging, because the "other" binary contains a copy of the
   211→            # architecture that the "host" platform provides.
   212→            #
   213→            # To avoid this - ensure that the libraries in the app packages for the "other"
   214→            # arch are all thin.
   215→            #
   216→            # This doesn't matter if it happens the other way around - if the "host" arch
   217→            # installs a universal binary, then the "other" arch won't be asked to install
   218→            # a binary at all.
   219→            self.thin_app_packages(other_app_packages_path, arch=other_arch)
   220→
   221→            # Merge the binaries
   222→            self.merge_app_packages(
   223→                target_app_packages=app_packages_path,
   224→                sources=[host_app_packages_path, other_app_packages_path],
   225→            )
   226→        else:
   227→            # If we're not building a universal binary, we can do a single install pass
   228→            # directly into the app_packages folder.
   229→            super()._install_app_requirements(
   230→                app,
   231→                requires=requires,
   232→                app_packages_path=app_packages_path,
   233→                pip_args=[
   234→                    "--only-binary",
   235→                    ":all:",
   236→                    "--platform",
   237→                    f"macosx_{macOS_min_tag}_{self.tools.host_arch}",
   238→                ],
   239→            )
   240→
   241→            # Since we're only targeting 1 architecture, we can strip any universal
   242→            # libraries down to just the host architecture.
   243→            self.thin_app_packages(app_packages_path, arch=self.tools.host_arch)

   325→    def run_console_app(
   326→        self,
   327→        app: AppConfig,
   328→        test_mode: bool,
   329→        passthrough: list[str],
   330→        **kwargs,
   331→    ):
   332→        """Start the console application.
   333→
   334→        :param app: The config object for the app
   335→        :param test_mode: Boolean; Is the app running in test mode?
   336→        :param passthrough: The list of arguments to pass to the app
   337→        """
   338→        sub_kwargs = self._prepare_app_kwargs(app=app, test_mode=test_mode)
   339→        cmdline = [self.binary_path(app) / f"Contents/MacOS/{app.formal_name}"]
   340→        cmdline.extend(passthrough)
   341→
   342→        if test_mode:
   343→            # Stream the app's output for testing.
   344→            # When a console app runs normally, its stdout should be connected
   345→            # directly to the terminal to properly display the app. When its test
   346→            # suite is running, though, Briefcase should stream the output to
   347→            # capture the testing outcome.
   348→            app_popen = self.tools.subprocess.Popen(
   349→                cmdline,
   350→                cwd=self.tools.home_path,
   351→                stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
   352→                stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
   353→                bufsize=1,
   354→                **sub_kwargs,
   355→            )
   356→            self._stream_app_logs(app, popen=app_popen, test_mode=test_mode)
   357→
   358→        else:
   359→            try:
   360→                # Start the app directly
   361→                self.console.info("=" * 75)
   362→                self.tools.subprocess.run(
   363→                    cmdline,
   364→                    cwd=self.tools.home_path,
   365→                    check=True,
   366→                    stream_output=False,
   367→                    **sub_kwargs,
   368→                )
   369→            except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
   370→                # The command line app *could* returns an error code, which is entirely legal.
   371→                # Ignore any subprocess error here.
   372→                pass

   374→    def run_gui_app(
   375→        self,
   376→        app: AppConfig,
   377→        test_mode: bool,
   378→        passthrough: list[str],
   379→        **kwargs,
   380→    ):
   381→        """Start the GUI application.
   382→
   383→        :param app: The config object for the app
   384→        :param test_mode: Boolean; Is the app running in test mode?
   385→        :param passthrough: The list of arguments to pass to the app
   386→        """
   387→        # Start log stream for the app.
   388→        # Streaming the system log is... a mess. The system log contains a
   389→        # *lot* of noise from other processes; even if you filter by
   390→        # process, there's a lot of macOS-generated noise. It's very
   391→        # difficult to extract just the "user generated" stdout/err log
   392→        # messages.
   393→        #
   394→        # The following sets up a log stream filter that looks for:
   395→        #  1. a log sender that matches that app binary; or,
   396→        #  2. a log sender of libffi, and a process that matches the app binary.
   397→        # Case (1) works for pre-Python 3.9 static linked binaries.
   398→        # Case (2) works for Python 3.9+ dynamic linked binaries.
   399→        # It's not enough to filter on *just* the processImagePath,
   400→        # as the process will generate lots of system-level messages.
   401→        # We can't filter on *just* the senderImagePath, because other
   402→        # apps will generate log messages that would be caught by the filter.
   403→        sender = os.fsdecode(self.binary_path(app) / "Contents/MacOS" / app.formal_name)
   404→        log_popen = self.tools.subprocess.Popen(
   405→            [
   406→                "log",
   407→                "stream",
   408→                "--style",
   409→                "compact",
   410→                "--predicate",
   411→                f'senderImagePath=="{sender}"'
   412→                f' OR (processImagePath=="{sender}"'
   413→                ' AND senderImagePath=="/usr/lib/libffi.dylib")',
   414→            ],
   415→            stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
   416→            stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
   417→            bufsize=1,
   418→        )
   419→
   420→        # Wait for the log stream start up
   421→        time.sleep(0.25)
   422→
   423→        app_pid = None
   424→        try:
   425→            # Set up the log stream
   426→            sub_kwargs = self._prepare_app_kwargs(app=app, test_mode=test_mode)
   427→
   428→            # Start the app in a way that lets us stream the logs
   429→            self.tools.subprocess.run(
   430→                # Force a new app to be launched
   431→                ["open", "-n", self.binary_path(app)]
   432→                + ((["--args"] + passthrough) if passthrough else []),
   433→                cwd=self.tools.home_path,
   434→                check=True,
   435→                **sub_kwargs,
   436→            )
   437→
   438→            # Find the App process ID so log streaming can exit when the app exits
   439→            app_pid = get_process_id_by_command(
   440→                command=str(self.binary_path(app)),
   441→                console=self.console,
   442→            )
   443→
   444→            if app_pid is None:
   445→                raise BriefcaseCommandError(
   446→                    f"Unable to find process for app {app.app_name} to start log streaming."
   447→                )
   448→
   449→            # Stream the app logs.
   450→            self._stream_app_logs(
   451→                app,
   452→                popen=log_popen,
   453→                test_mode=test_mode,
   454→                clean_filter=macOS_log_clean_filter,
   455→                clean_output=True,
   456→                stop_func=lambda: is_process_dead(app_pid),
   457→                log_stream=True,
   458→            )
   459→        except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
   460→            raise BriefcaseCommandError(f"Unable to start app {app.app_name}.")
   461→        finally:
   462→            # Ensure the App also terminates when exiting
   463→            if app_pid:  # pragma: no-cover-if-is-py310
   464→                with suppress(ProcessLookupError):
   465→                    self.tools.os.kill(app_pid, SIGTERM)

   468→def is_mach_o_binary(path):  # pragma: no-cover-if-is-windows
   469→    """Determine if the file at the given path is a Mach-O binary.
   470→
   471→    :param path: The path to check
   472→    :returns: True if the file at the given location is a Mach-O binary.
   473→    """
   474→    # A binary is any file that is executable, or has a suffix from a known list
   475→    if os.access(path, os.X_OK) or path.suffix.lower() in {".dylib", ".o", ".so", ""}:
   476→        # File is a binary; read the file magic to determine if it's Mach-O.
   477→        with path.open("rb") as f:
   478→            magic = f.read(4)
   479→            return magic in (
   480→                b"\xca\xfe\xba\xbe",
   481→                b"\xcf\xfa\xed\xfe",
   482→                b"\xce\xfa\xed\xfe",
   483→                b"\xbe\xba\xfe\xca",
   484→                b"\xfe\xed\xfa\xcf",
   485→                b"\xfe\xed\xfa\xce",
   486→            )
   487→    else:
   488→        # Not a binary
   489→        return False

   658→    def sign_app(
   659→        self,
   660→        app: AppConfig,
   661→        identity: SigningIdentity,
   662→    ):  # pragma: no-cover-if-is-windows
   663→        """Sign an entire app with a specific identity.
   664→
   665→        :param app: The app to sign
   666→        :param identity: The signing identity to use
   667→        """
   668→        bundle_path = self.binary_path(app)
   669→        resources_path = bundle_path / "Contents/Resources"
   670→        frameworks_path = bundle_path / "Contents/Frameworks"
   671→
   672→        sign_targets = []
   673→
   674→        for folder in (resources_path, frameworks_path):
   675→            # Sign all Mach-O executable objects
   676→            sign_targets.extend(
   677→                path
   678→                for path in folder.rglob("*")
   679→                if not path.is_dir()
   680→                and not path.is_symlink()
   681                and is_mach_o_binary(path)
   682→            )
   683→
   684→            # Sign all embedded frameworks
   685→            sign_targets.extend(folder.rglob("*.framework"))
   686→
   687→            # Sign all embedded app objects
   688→            sign_targets.extend(folder.rglob("*.app"))
   689→
   690→        # Sign the bundle path itself
   691→        sign_targets.append(bundle_path)
   692→
   693→        # Run signing through a ThreadPoolExecutor so that they run in parallel. We need
   694→        # to ensure that objects are signed from the inside out (i.e., a folder must be
   695→        # signed *after* all it's contents has been signed; files in a folder must be
   696→        # signed *after* all subfolders in that same folder); and an app that uses a
   697→        # library must be signed *after* all the libraries it uses. See
   698→        # https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode/creating-distribution-signed-code-for-the-mac#Determine-the-signing-order
   699→        # for details.
   700→        #
   701→        # To do this, we utilize grouping on a sorted list, and rely on the fact that a
   702→        # new group is created whenever the grouping key changes. The sorting process
   703→        # guarantees depth-first ordering; the grouping is applied over the sorted
   704→        # content, ensuring that that folders are signed before files.
   705→        #
   706→        # This approach isn't perfect. It will fail if there's an embedded app that uses
   707→        # a library in a different framework, and the app is lexically sorted before the
   708→        # library (e.g. if app_packages/foobar/Alpha.framework/Helpers/My App.app
   709→        # depends on app_packages/footbar/Beta.framework/libbeta). However, if you're
   710→        # embedding apps in frameworks in Python libraries that are installed by pip,
   711→        # you're already making poor life choices; this approach is enough to satisfy
   712→        # the one use of app-in-framework embedding that we're aware of (PySide).
   713→        progress_bar = self.console.progress_bar()
   714→        task_id = progress_bar.add_task("Signing App", total=len(sign_targets))
   715→        with progress_bar:
   716→            for group in self.tools.file.sorted_depth_first_groups(sign_targets):
   717→                with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(
   718→                    max_workers=1 if self.console.is_deep_debug else None
   719→                ) as executor:
   720→                    futures = []
   721→                    for path in group:
   722→                        future = executor.submit(
   723→                            self.sign_file,
   724→                            path,
   725→                            entitlements=self.entitlements_path(app),
   726→                            identity=identity,
   727→                        )
   728→                        futures.append(future)
   729→                    for future in concurrent.futures.as_completed(futures):
   730→                        progress_bar.update(task_id, advance=1)
   731→                        if future.exception():
   732→                            raise future.exception()

   328→    def _download_support_package(self, app: AppConfig):
   329→        try:
   330→            # Work out if the app defines a custom override for
   331→            # the support package URL.
   332→            try:
   333→                support_package_url = app.support_package
   334→                custom_support_package = True
   335→                self.console.info(f"Using custom support package {support_package_url}")
   336→                try:
   337→                    # If the app has a custom support package *and* a support revision,
   338→                    # that's an error.
   339→                    app.support_revision
   340→                    self.console.warning(
   341→                        "App specifies both a support package and a support revision; "
   342→                        "support revision will be ignored."
   343→                    )
   344→                except AttributeError:
   345→                    pass
   346→            except AttributeError:
   347→                # If the app specifies a support revision, use it;
   348→                # otherwise, use the support revision named by the template
   349→                try:
   350→                    support_revision = app.support_revision
   351→                except AttributeError:
   352→                    # No support revision specified; use the template-specified version
   353→                    try:
   354→                        support_revision = self.support_revision(app)
   355→                    except KeyError:
   356→                        # No template-specified support revision
   357→                        raise MissingSupportPackage(
   358→                            python_version_tag=self.python_version_tag,
   359→                            platform=self.platform,
   360→                            host_arch=self.tools.host_arch,
   361→                            is_32bit=self.tools.is_32bit_python,
   362→                        )
   363→
   364→                support_package_url = self.support_package_url(support_revision)
   365→                custom_support_package = False
   366→                self.console.info(f"Using support package {support_package_url}")
   367→
   368→            if support_package_url.startswith(("https://", "http://")):
   369→                if custom_support_package:
   370→                    # If the support package is custom, cache it using a hash of
   371→                    # the download URL. This is needed to differentiate to support
   372→                    # packages with the same filename, served at different URLs.
   373→                    # (or a custom package that collides with an official package name)
   374→                    download_path = (
   375→                        self.data_path
   376→                        / "support"
   377→                        / hashlib.sha256(
   378→                            support_package_url.encode("utf-8")
   379→                        ).hexdigest()
   380→                    )
   381→                else:
   382→                    download_path = self.data_path / "support"
   383→
   384→                # Download the support file, caching the result
   385→                # in the user's briefcase support cache directory.
   386→                return self.tools.file.download(
   387→                    url=support_package_url,
   388→                    download_path=download_path,
   389→                    role="support package",
   390→                )
   391→            else:
   392→                return Path(support_package_url)
   393→        except MissingNetworkResourceError as e:
   394→            # If there is a custom support package, report the missing resource as-is.
   395→            if custom_support_package:
   396→                raise
   397→            else:
   398→                raise MissingSupportPackage(
   399→                    python_version_tag=self.python_version_tag,
   400→                    platform=self.platform,
   401→                    host_arch=self.tools.host_arch,
   402→                    is_32bit=self.tools.is_32bit_python,
   403→                ) from e

  1017→def _has_url(requirement):
  1018→    """Determine if the requirement is defined as a URL.
  1019→
  1020→    Detects any of the URL schemes supported by pip
  1021→    (https://pip.pypa.io/en/stable/topics/vcs-support/).
  1022→
  1023→    :param requirement: The requirement to check
  1024→    :returns: True if the requirement is a URL supported by pip.
  1025→    """
  1026→    return any(
  1027→        f"{scheme}:" in requirement
  1028→        for scheme in (
  1029→            ["http", "https", "file", "ftp"]
  1030→            + ["git+file", "git+https", "git+ssh", "git+http", "git+git", "git"]
  1031→            + ["hg+file", "hg+http", "hg+https", "hg+ssh", "hg+static-http"]
  1032→            + ["svn", "svn+svn", "svn+http", "svn+https", "svn+ssh"]
  1033→            + ["bzr+http", "bzr+https", "bzr+ssh", "bzr+sftp", "bzr+ftp", "bzr+lp"]
  1034→        )
  1035→    )

  1038→def _is_local_path(reference):

  1040→
  1041→    :param reference: The reference to check
  1042→    :returns: True if the reference is a local file path
  1043→    """
  1044→    # Windows allows both / and \ as a path separator in references.
  1045→    separators = [os.sep]
  1046→    if os.altsep:
  1047→        separators.append(os.altsep)

  1049→    return any(sep in reference for sep in separators) and (not _has_url(reference))
